cards.text: Jacob's on his way home, and word comes that his brother Esau is coming to meet him with four hundred men. Jacob is in great fear and distress. He sends herd after herd of gifts ahead of him and spends the night in camp.
During the night, Jacob gets up and takes his two wives, his two maidservants and his eleven sons across the ford of the Jabbok. He sends them over the stream with everything he owns.

cards.question: After sending everyone across the Jabbok, Jacob keeps a few servants with him for the night.

cards.text: So Jacob is left all alone, and there a man wrestles with him. I spent YEARS in the dark in a junk drawer, friend, and the roughest thing that ever jumped me was a rubber band.

cards.question: How long does the man keep wrestling with Jacob?
When the man sees he can't overpower Jacob, he strikes the socket of Jacob's ___.

cards.text: Jacob's hip is dislocated, and the man says, “Let me go, for it is daybreak.” If MY hip popped out, friend, I'd let go of the man, the fight, my hat, EVERYTHING.

cards.question: Jacob says he won't let the man go unless he gets something first. What is it?
Before anything else happens, the man asks Jacob his ___.

cards.text: “Jacob,” he replies, and the man says his name will no longer be Jacob. Most folks need a stack of forms and a LONG line to change their name, friend, and Jacob gets it done mid-wrestle.

cards.question: What new name does the man give Jacob?
Why the name Israel, according to the man who wrestled Jacob?

answers.text: Jacob has struggled with God and with men and prevailed
Jacob has run from God and from men and escaped
Jacob has pleased God and men and been honored

cards.text: Now Jacob asks, “Please tell me your name.” Fair enough, friend, because if you wrestle somebody ALL NIGHT, you want to know who it is.

cards.question: When Jacob asks, the man tells Jacob his name.
Instead the man asks, “Why do you ask my name?” Then he ___ Jacob there.
Jacob names the place Peniel. What reason does he give?

answers.text: He has seen God face to face and his life was spared
He has won the hardest fight of his whole life
He has finally made peace with his brother Esau

cards.text: The sun rises above Jacob as he passes by Penuel. Friend, the man started the night ALONE by a stream and heads off at sunrise with a NEW NAME.

cards.question: How is Jacob getting around as the sun rises over him?

answers.text: Riding on one of his camels

cards.question: Because of Jacob's hip, the Israelites to this day don't eat the tendon attached to the socket of the hip.

cards.text: Hang on to your apron, friend. Jacob's story keeps going, and I'm not saying another WORD about it yet.

findings.problem: The statement says Jacob sends "everyone" across the Jabbok, then asks whether he keeps a few servants with him. If everyone was sent across, no one could stay, so the question's own wording rules out True and gives away the answer.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Most choice cards can't be reasoned out from the earlier cards. Card 5 (until daybreak), card 6 (hip), card 8 (a blessing), card 9 (name), card 11 (Israel), card 14 (the man doesn't give his name) and card 19 (the tendon) are all discovery questions. That is 7 of the 12 choice cards. Only cards 3, 12, 15, 16 and 18 are informed guesses. The setup story cards need more context, or some of these questions should be swapped for questions the baker can reason out.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The card says Jacob "started the night ALONE by a stream." The text shows otherwise. Jacob spent the night in the camp (32:21), got up during the night with his wives, maidservants and sons, and crossed the ford with them (32:22-23). Only after that was he left alone (32:24). The card also calls Jacob "the man," which is the word every earlier card used for the wrestler, so the baker may not know who it means.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: Card 20 holds only the line saying the story isn't over and tells nothing from the passage. It still cites Genesis 32:32, a verse already cited by choice card 19.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the line saying the story isn't over, what should its "verses" field cite? Should it cite the passage's last verse, nothing, or something else? The rule that every story card cites the verses it tells doesn't fit a card that tells no verses.
